differences.what: massing: the draft's flat-roofed stone-front box is now the photograph's front: the north part under a slated mansard rising from a stone cornice, the south part carried up as a projection under a steep gable, the porch between them; the mansard's curb prints at y 230 px as the photograph's, the gable's apex at y 85 against 70 (0.15 m)
every street light: the north part's two pairs a storey and the light over the porch, and the projection's two pairs, print within about 10 px of the photograph's in place, width and height

the dormers: two gabled dormers on the mansard on the axes the photograph gives them, a pair of lights in the north one and one in the other, their pediments standing up over the curb, the north one's pilasters at x 52-240 px and the south one's at x 382-505 as the photograph's (T-3634 re-read their widths off the pilasters: 2.06 and 1.36 m)

the dormers' dress (T-3634): each is now the photograph's classical pediment in the front's stone: a pilaster with its capital either side of the lights, a frieze over them, a level cornice 0.25 m deep returned past the pilasters, its top 0.55 m over the lights' heads as the photograph's (50 px), the raking cornice in two bands pitched 45 degrees, and in each tympanum a carved lunette standing on the level cornice, a moulded ring round a fan of leaves and a boss at their foot, 0.38 and 0.28 m in radius against about 0.38 and 0.28 m (x 117-180 and 422-470 px). The capitals' carving and the fan's own carving are under the bar

the dormers' height: the whole dormer, lights, cornice, lunette and apex together, prints about 20 px (0.2 m) over the photograph's: the render's lights run y 295-385 against 312-400 px and its level cornice tops out at y 245 against 262. K01 stands a dormer's light at least 0.1 m over its face's foot on the lower face, where the photograph's lights run down behind the main cornice; the record takes that least sill and the face's least setback. Under the bar

the cresting: the photograph's crest along the mansard's curb is a row of square crenellations (y 222-240 px), merlons about 13-14 px wide at about 31 px centres over a solid band; the render's is now the deck's crenellated iron cresting, merlons 0.15 m wide at 0.34 m centres rising 0.09 m over a band, 0.2 m in all, printing along the curb in the photograph's rhythm and stopping either side of each dormer as the photograph's does (T-3634; it was K10's iron scroll cresting, a different shape)
the main cornice: the photograph's is a deep cornice with a row of blocks under it (y 410-470 px); the render's is K10's moulded stone cornice without the blocks, shallower by about 0.2 m

the projection's gable: the photograph's has projecting bargeboards and a dentilled band across its foot (y 360-420 px) with a ventilator in its peak; the render's is K08's coped gable with a kneeler at each foot and no band across

the gable's two attic lights (x 667-730 and 750-812 px, y 240-350): now cut in the gable's face, side by side either side of its middle, their heads at y 240 against 237 px and their sills at y 340 against 350, each about 55 px across against 60 (T-3634: K08's coped gable takes square-headed lights in its face). They print about 25 px south of the photograph's with the gable itself, whose apex stands at x 759 against 733 (the projection's place, 0.3 m, the camera fit's soft depth), and their sashes are the house's two-over-two in green where the print shows them dark: under the bar
the porch: two columns with carved capitals carrying a stone deck at the photograph's height (render y 655-710 against 665-700 px), on a stoop between newels; built 2.6 m wide against about 2.8 m

the porch's parapet (T-3634): now the photograph's coped solid band pierced with five rings across its front (render y 665-690 px against 675-695, at the photograph's spacing), between corner pedestals, each front pedestal carrying a ball finial on a square plinth (render y 610-650 against 608-660 px); K01's hood railing takes a pierced band in place of balusters. The parapet's top prints about 10 px (0.1 m) over the photograph's coping, and its returns, which the picture does not see, are pierced at the front's spacing
the door: the photograph's opening is dark and deep, with a glazed double door and a transom; the render's is a single panelled leaf in a reveal

the basement: lights under each pair of the ground storey's windows, as the photograph's, every one barred: the projection's two now carry the north part's grille in their K08 reveals, its ring 0.15 m against the north part's 0.1 m (T-3634: at 0.1 m the ring's legs lay on the third and fifth of its seven bars, the face drawn twice that refused it before; 5 cm, under the bar). They stand 0.2-0.8 m over the walk against about 0.33-1.04 m (0.24 m at the head), under the bar

the north stack (T-3634): now on the mansard's cornice astride the flank wall, where the photograph's left edge puts it (render x 0-35 px at the frame's edge against 0-50, its top at y 85 against 80); K01's mansard deck now lets a stack on the cornice stand through its curb, its cresting stopping either side. Until T-3634 it stood 0.7 m inside the flank and 0.4 m low
the railing: the photograph shows a low iron railing along the front's foot before the basement; the render's is the parcel's iron spear fence on the street line, which stands taller in the frame
the stone's colour and the windows' paint: the print is monochrome
the flanks, the rear and the rear range: the photograph is square to the front
